entries.settings: Unsupervised fit on full series; sliding-window embedding with FFT-based window length; scores min-max normalized; point-wise AUC-ROC averaged over all 367 YAHOO series

source.title: TSB-UAD: An End-to-End Benchmark Suite for Univariate Time-Series Anomaly Detection (Paparrizos et al.)
source.locator: README 'Overall Results' table, row YAHOO, column LOF (AUC 0.86, F 0.62)

entries.notes: Granularity gap: the paper value averages 367 Yahoo series; the labts yahoo dataset is a single bundled series (1000 points, 7 anomalies). Directional check only.
entries.command: python playground/labts.py run --task anomaly_detection --algorithm registered-anomaly_detection-PyODLOFDetector --dataset yahoo --metric auc_roc --compact

entries.settings: Original NOTEARS (least-squares + L1 + acyclicity); full dataset n=7466, no train/test split; SHD vs the 20-edge consensus DAG; 16 edges estimated

source.title: DAGs with NO TEARS: Continuous Optimization for Structure Learning (Zheng, Aragam, Ravikumar, Xing)
source.locator: Section 5.4 'Real-data': '16 for NOTEARS with an SHD of 22'

entries.notes: Same continuous Sachs data and same 20-edge consensus DAG as the paper (vendored from cmu-phil/example-causal-datasets). labts must run with max_samples=7466 (default subsample is 2000).
entries.command: python playground/labts.py run --task causal --algorithm causal-notears --dataset causal-sachs-cont --param max_samples=7466 --compact

entries.settings: PC in Tetrad 7.6.7 with default settings; CPDAG with 24 estimated edges; SHD vs the 20-edge ground-truth DAG

source.title: Are You Doing Better Than Random Guessing? A Call for Using Negative Controls When Evaluating Causal Discovery Algorithms (Petersen)
source.locator: Table 6 'SHD for the Sachs Data', row PC

entries.notes: Implementation gap: paper uses Tetrad's PC; labts uses causal-learn's PC. Independence-test defaults may differ.
entries.command: python playground/labts.py run --task causal --algorithm causal-pc --dataset causal-sachs-cont --param max_samples=7466 --compact

entries.settings: GES in Tetrad 7.6.7 with default settings; CPDAG with 30 estimated edges; SHD vs the 20-edge ground-truth DAG

source.title: Are You Doing Better Than Random Guessing? A Call for Using Negative Controls When Evaluating Causal Discovery Algorithms (Petersen)
source.locator: Table 6 'SHD for the Sachs Data', row GES

entries.notes: Implementation gap: Tetrad GES vs causal-learn GES. (The NOTEARS paper reports FGS SHD=22 on the same data; Tetrad GES defaults give 30.)
entries.command: python playground/labts.py run --task causal --algorithm causal-ges --dataset causal-sachs-cont --param max_samples=7466 --compact

entries.settings: UCR default train/test split (67/1029); 10,000 random kernels; RidgeClassifierCV(alphas=logspace(-3,3,10), normalize=True); mean over 10 runs (std 0.001)

source.title: ROCKET: Exceptionally Fast and Accurate Time Series Classification Using Random Convolutional Kernels (Dempster, Petitjean, Webb)
source.locator: official results_ucr.csv, row ItalyPowerDemand, accuracy_mean column

entries.notes: sktime RocketClassifier matches the paper protocol (10,000 kernels + RidgeClassifierCV). Kernels are random, so single-run accuracy varies within the paper's reported std (~0.001).
entries.command: python playground/labts.py run --task classification --algorithm registered-classification-RocketClassifier --dataset italy-power-demand --metric accuracy --compact

entries.settings: UCR default train/test split (36/175); 10,000 random kernels; RidgeClassifierCV; mean over 10 runs (std 0.0094)

source.title: ROCKET: Exceptionally Fast and Accurate Time Series Classification Using Random Convolutional Kernels (Dempster, Petitjean, Webb)
source.locator: official results_ucr.csv, row ArrowHead, accuracy_mean column

entries.notes: Non-saturated dataset; paper std over 10 runs is ~0.0094, so +/-0.03 tolerance covers kernel randomness.
entries.command: python playground/labts.py run --task classification --algorithm registered-classification-RocketClassifier --dataset arrow-head --metric accuracy --compact

entries.settings: k=3 (= number of classes); full dataset clustered (train+test fused, N=211); mean over 10 runs of the authors' Matlab implementation

source.title: k-Shape: Efficient and Accurate Clustering of Time Series (Paparrizos & Gravano) — official Matlab repository
source.locator: README 'Results on the 128 univariate datasets', row ArrowHead (RI 0.623006, ARI 0.17425450, NMI 0.2533444)

entries.notes: Paper value is the mean of 10 Matlab runs; labts runs tslearn's KShape once with a fixed seed. Random init makes single-run ARI swing; RI=0.623006 in the same row.
entries.command: python playground/labts.py run --task clustering --algorithm registered-clustering-TimeSeriesKShapes --dataset arrow-head-cl --param n_clusters=3 --param random_state=42 --metric ari --compact

entries.settings: k=2 (= number of classes); full dataset clustered (train+test fused, N=306); mean over 10 runs of the authors' Matlab implementation

source.title: k-Shape: Efficient and Accurate Clustering of Time Series (Paparrizos & Gravano) — official Matlab repository
source.locator: README 'Results on the 128 univariate datasets', row GunPoint (RI 0.497487, ARI -0.005050, NMI 0.0)

entries.notes: GunPoint clustering is at chance level even for the authors (RI 0.4975, NMI 0.0) — reproducing this row validates that near-chance behavior, not a bug.
entries.command: python playground/labts.py run --task clustering --algorithm registered-clustering-TimeSeriesKShapes --dataset gunpoint-cl --param n_clusters=2 --param random_state=42 --metric ari --compact

entries.settings: Multivariate LTSF-Linear protocol; look-back L=336, horizon 96; z-score normalized; test-set MSE averaged over 7 channels and rolling origins over the 4-month test split

source.title: Are Transformers Effective for Time Series Forecasting? (Zeng et al.)
source.locator: Table 2, row ETTh1/96, DLinear* (authors' own run)

entries.notes: Protocol gap: paper trains on a 12-month split and evaluates rolling-origin over the 4-month test set across all 7 channels; labts trains on all but the last 96 points and scores a single univariate origin with num_epochs=3. Expect deviation until rolling-origin multivariate evaluation lands.
entries.command: python playground/labts.py run --task forecasting --algorithm registered-forecasting-DLinearForecaster --dataset hf-etth1 --param seq_len=336 --param pred_len=96 --param horizon=96 --metric mse --compact

entries.settings: Multivariate LTSF-Linear protocol; look-back L=336, horizon 96; z-score normalized; test-set MSE averaged over 21 channels and rolling origins

source.title: Are Transformers Effective for Time Series Forecasting? (Zeng et al.)

entries.notes: Same protocol gap as the ETTh1 entry (univariate single-origin holdout vs multivariate rolling-origin test).
entries.command: python playground/labts.py run --task forecasting --algorithm registered-forecasting-DLinearForecaster --dataset hf-weather --param seq_len=336 --param pred_len=96 --param horizon=96 --metric mse --compact

entries.settings: Multivariate LTSF protocol; look-back L=96 (Transformers), horizon 96; z-score normalized; test-set MSE

source.title: Are Transformers Effective for Time Series Forecasting? (Zeng et al.)
source.locator: Table 2, row ETTh1/96, Autoformer (quoted from the FEDformer paper, ICML 2022; identical to Autoformer paper's own value)

entries.notes: Same protocol gap as the DLinear entries; also num_epochs=3 default (paper trains to convergence).
entries.command: python playground/labts.py run --task forecasting --algorithm registered-forecasting-AutoformerForecaster --dataset hf-etth1 --param seq_len=96 --param pred_len=96 --param horizon=96 --metric mse --compact

entries.settings: TSER archive default train/test split (140/61); ROCKET transform with ridge-regression-style regressor; average RMSE over 5 runs

source.title: Time Series Extrinsic Regression (Tan, Bergmeir, Petitjean, Webb) — official TSER results page
source.venue: Data Mining and Knowledge Discovery 35, 2021 / tseregression.org
source.locator: Results table, row Covid3Month, column Rocket

entries.notes: Rocket was the best-ranked algorithm in the TSER paper. sktime RocketRegressor follows the same protocol (fixed archive split, ridge on ROCKET features).
entries.command: python playground/labts.py run --task regression --algorithm registered-regression-RocketRegressor --dataset covid-3month --metric rmse --compact

entries.settings: TSER archive default train/test split (140/61); scikit-learn RandomForest with default parameters on the flattened raw series; average RMSE over 5 runs

source.title: Time Series Extrinsic Regression (Tan, Bergmeir, Petitjean, Webb) — official TSER results page
source.venue: Data Mining and Knowledge Discovery 35, 2021 / tseregression.org
source.locator: Results table, row Covid3Month, column RandomForest

entries.notes: Protocol mismatch on purpose: the paper flattens the raw series into sklearn defaults, while the labts pipeline fits RF(25 trees) on summary features. Kept as a demonstration that the leaderboard flags representation gaps, not only implementation bugs.
entries.command: python playground/labts.py run --task regression --algorithm summary-random-forest-regressor --dataset covid-3month --metric rmse --compact
